# SKELETON - Sources

Nine repositories, verified on 2026-11-25. Star counts are approximate and were
read from the GitHub API (or the repository page where the API rate limit hit).
Split: 4 gamedev, 3 software development, 2 AI-agent workflow.

No code, file, or license was copied. Each entry states what was borrowed as an
idea and what was rejected.

## Gamedev (4)

### S1. phaserjs/template-vite-ts

- URL: https://github.com/phaserjs/template-vite-ts
- Stars: ~200 (198); last push 2026-04-21; not archived.
- Artifact: official Phaser + TypeScript + Vite project template.
- Analogous: the minimal runnable game repo that a generator copies.
- Borrowed: the root stays tiny (config, `src/`, `public/`); build output is
  ignored, not committed; the README is a start/run/build document, not a spec.
- Rejected: engine code and bundler config inside the template. In gamefirst the
  engine is a pack; the skeleton must stay engine-free.

### S2. godotengine/godot-demo-projects

- URL: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects
- Stars: ~9.8k (9,838); last push 2026-11-25; not archived.
- Artifact: official collection of small, self-contained demo projects.
- Analogous: proof that a project tree can be read and copied without a manifest.
- Borrowed: one directory per self-contained unit, a short index at the top, and
  each unit small enough to read in one sitting.
- Rejected: binary assets committed per demo and no documentation discipline.
  gamefirst tracks evidence deliberately and documents only what works.

### S3. libgdx/gdx-liftoff

- URL: https://github.com/libgdx/gdx-liftoff
- Stars: ~700 (696); last push 2026-11-24; not archived.
- Artifact: GUI/CLI project generator that writes a libGDX skeleton from options.
- Analogous: `new-project` (CLI01) - a generator that copies a base tree and adds
  the selected parts.
- Borrowed: the base tree is the default, options are additive, and the generator
  writes the resulting versions into a file inside the project (the lockfile
  idea). A generated project must build without the generator.
- Rejected: a GUI wizard and language-specific templates. gamefirst selects packs
  on the command line and keeps the skeleton engine-neutral.

### S4. TheBevyFlock/bevy_new_2d

- URL: https://github.com/TheBevyFlock/bevy_new_2d
- Stars: ~500; 402 commits, 75 forks; active in 2026 (per repository page; the
  API rate limit blocked `pushed_at`).
- Artifact: a 2D game template generated by `bevy new`, with `*.template` files,
  `cargo-generate.toml`, and a `post-generate.rhai` hook.
- Analogous: a template that is also a generator input, with a documented design
  rationale in `docs/design.md`.
- Borrowed: the idea of marking files that the generator must rewrite (name,
  version) instead of shipping placeholders everywhere; a `docs/` folder that
  explains structure rather than duplicating it; a short "where to put what"
  table in the README.
- Rejected: committing editor state (`.vscode/`, `.idea/`) and engine code in the
  template root. Both are ignored or moved to a pack here.

## Software development (3)

### S5. jsynowiec/node-typescript-boilerplate

- URL: https://github.com/jsynowiec/node-typescript-boilerplate
- Stars: ~3.0k (2,964); last push 2026-10-30; not archived.
- Artifact: production-ready Node + TypeScript project skeleton with tests, lint,
  format, and CI.
- Analogous: the `package.json` script surface that a "verify" command calls.
- Borrowed: one obvious command per job (`build`, `test`, `lint`), tests in
  `tests/` outside `src/`, and config files that are short enough to read.
- Rejected: the toolchain stack itself (Vitest, Oxlint, pnpm, Mise). The engine
  pack owns tools; the skeleton must not pick one.

### S6. github/gitignore

- URL: https://github.com/github/gitignore
- Stars: ~176k (176,457); last push 2026-11-24; not archived.
- Artifact: the canonical collection of `.gitignore` templates (Node, Global,
  macOS, Windows).
- Analogous: the exact artifact under review here, at the line level.
- Borrowed: entries from `Node.gitignore` and `Global/` (OS and editor noise);
  the principle that every ignore line answers "what generates this and where
  does it come from".
- Rejected: copying whole templates. A game repo needs a short list it can
  defend, not a 40-line union of every editor.

### S7. cookiecutter/cookiecutter

- URL: https://github.com/cookiecutter/cookiecutter
- Stars: ~25k (25,184); last push 2026-04-01; not archived.
- Artifact: a project-template engine: a plain directory tree plus a context file
  and optional hooks.
- Analogous: how `new-project` copies `template/` and then adds packs.
- Borrowed: the template is a normal directory tree that a human can read and
  edit without the generator; substitution is a thin post-step, not a custom
  runtime format. Empty directories are materialised by a placeholder file.
- Rejected: templating every file with a variable language. The skeleton has one
  substitution (the game name) and does not need a template dialect.

## AI-agent workflow (2)

### S8. github/spec-kit

- URL: https://github.com/github/spec-kit
- Stars: ~151k (151,355); last push 2026-11-25; not archived.
- Artifact: spec-driven development toolkit: a constitution, a template per
  artifact, and one slash command per phase.
- Analogous: the instruction layer of a repo - short commands that point at
  templates instead of embedding them.
- Borrowed: a short, numbered constitution at the root; one command per step with
  a single responsibility; each phase leaves one named artifact behind; the
  command text stays thin because the template holds the detail.
- Rejected: the ceremony of a fixed multi-document pipeline per feature. gamefirst
  writes one page per document and only after the mechanic works.

### S9. bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD

- URL: https://github.com/bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD
- Stars: ~56k (55,731); last push 2026-11-25; not archived.
- Artifact: agent-based development method: role agents, workflows, and
  scale-adaptive planning documents.
- Analogous: routing work between roles and keeping the working documents small.
- Borrowed: scale-adaptive depth (a small change gets a short path), a named owner
  per document, and the rule that an agent reads the artifact instead of
  re-deriving it.
- Rejected: a standing multi-agent council and the document set it produces. That
  is a blueprint non-goal; crews here are temporary.

## Dead ends

- `ourcade/phaser3-typescript-vite-template` (137 stars) was the first choice for
  S1. It was dropped: last push 2023-01, so it no longer represents current
  practice. Its test/CI layout was the only thing worth borrowing, and S5 covers
  that better.
- `game-ci/unity-actions` was considered for a CI artifact. Rejected: the
  skeleton ships no CI (the release pack, P01, owns the build pipeline), so there
  was no analogous artifact to compare against.
- GitHub API rate limit (60 requests/hour, unauthenticated) blocked `pushed_at`
  for S4. The repository page was used instead; the star count and commit count
  come from there.
